name: Alaska Purchase 1867
notes: President Andrew Johnson signed a treaty with Russia on May 28, and the Alaska Territory was officially transferred to the United States on October 18, 1867. Purchased from Russia for $7.2 million in gold, critics at the time called the purchase "Seward's Folly". This purchase ended Russia’s presence in North America and ensured U.S. access to the Pacific northern rim.

name: British Cession 1818
notes: Acquired via the Convention of 1818 between the United States and Great Britain.  The Convention of 1818 was a treaty between the United States and Britain that set the 49th parallel of latitude as the boundary between British North America and the US across the West. This remains the boundary today between the two nations.

name: East Florida (Spanish Cession) 1819
notes: Secretary of State John Quincy Adams negotiated the acquisition of the Florida territory from Spain via the Adams-Onis Treaty. While the Americans didn't pay Spain for the land, they did agree to assume $5 million in damage caused by American citizens when they rebelled against Spain

name: Gadsden Purchase 1853
notes: The Gadsden Purchase, or Treaty, was an agreement between the United States and Mexico. Finalized in 1854, the United States agreed to pay Mexico $10 million for a 29,670 square mile portion of Mexico that later became part of Arizona and New Mexico. Gadsden’s Purchase provided the land necessary for a southern transcontinental railroad and attempted to resolve conflicts that lingered after the

name: Hawaii Annexation 1898
notes: The Hawaiian Islands were annexed as the Territory of Hawaii on July 7, 1898, despite opposition from Hawaiian Queen Lili'uokalani and native Hawaiians. The Queen had been overthrown by American sugar plantation owners, supported by U.S. Marines. The coup was declared illegal by President Cleveland, and initially, many senators didn't support annexation. Then, on February 15, 1898, the U.S. Battleship Maine was blown up in Havana Harbor in Cuba. The ensuing Spanish-American War, part of which was fought in the Philippine Islands, convinced the U.S. government that the Hawaiian islands would be strategically valuable as a mid-Pacific fueling station and naval installation. The annexation was passed, and over 50 years later, in March 1959, Hawaii became a state.

name: Louisiana Purchase 1803
notes: The Louisiana Purchase encompassed 530,000,000 acres of territory in North America that the United States purchased from France in 1803 for $15 million.

name: Louisiana Purchase 1803 / Ceded to Great Britain 1818
notes: This portion of the Louisiana Purchase was ceded to Great Britain as a result of the Convention of 1818. The Convention of 1818 was a treaty between the United States and Britain that set the 49th parallel of latitude as the boundary between British North America and the US across the West.

name: Louisiana Purchase 1803 / Mexican Cession 1848
notes: This portion of the Louisiana Purchase was disputed until 1848. The United States gained the Mexican Cession under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which ended the Mexican-American War in 1848. The cession was a stretch of territory from the Pacific Northwest through the American Southwest. It included contemporary states, including California, Arizona, New Mexico, Utah, Nevada, and Colorado.

name: Louisiana Purchase 1803 / Texas Annexation 1845
notes: This territory was annexed by the U.S. as part of the Texas Annexation in 1845. The Texas territory, primarily settled by Americans, wanted to separate from Mexico, but this action threatened war between the U.S. and Mexico. In 1844, Congress finally agreed to annex Texas. On December 29, 1845, Texas entered the United States as a slave state, broadening the irrepressible differences in the United States over the issue of slavery and setting off the Mexican-American War.

name: Mexican Cession 1848
notes: The Mexican Cession was part of the Treaty of Guadaloupe Hidalgo, which ended the Mexican-American War. Under the treaty, signed on February 2, 1848, Mexico ceded 55 percent of its territory, including the present-day states California, Nevada, Utah, New Mexico, most of Arizona and Colorado, and parts of Oklahoma, Kansas, and Wyoming. Mexico also relinquished all claims to Texas, and recognized the Rio Grande as the southern boundary with the United States. In return, the U.S. government paid Mexico $15 million

name: Oregon Territory 1846
notes: Originally Spain, Great Britain, Russia, and the United States all claimed the Oregon Territory. By 1843, increased American immigration on the Oregon Trail to the Territory made the border issue important to Congress. President James Polk, a supporter of Manifest Destiny, proposed a settlement on the 49 degree line to Great Britain. With some minor modifications, which reserved the whole of Vancouver Island to Canada, Great Britain agreed to Polk’s suggestion.

name: Territory of the Original Thirteen States (Ceded by Great Britain) 1783
notes: The original land of the U.S. was ceded by Great Britain in 1783 following the Revolutionary War. The Treaty of Paris, signed on September 3, 1783, ended the American Revolution and formally recognized the United States as an independent nation.
